rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is exhaling breath and shahīq its return; both terms can denote either the start or end of a donkey’s bray.
rows.anchor: الزفير إخراج النفس والشهيق رده، واستعمالها في أول النهيق وآخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired sounds signify extreme anguish, like heat gripping the heart and trapping the breath within it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهما الدلالة على شدة كربهم وغمهم وتشبيه حالهم بمن استولت الحرارة على قلبه وانحصر فيه روحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their cries may also be likened to the sounds of donkeys.
rows.anchor: أو تشبيه صراخهم بأصوات الحمير

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A reading pronounces شقوا with ḍamma on its initial consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { شقوا } بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase does not tie punishment to the heavens’ duration: revealed texts establish the damned’s endless stay and the heavens’ eventual end.
rows.anchor: ليس لارتباط دوامهم في النار بدوامهما فإن النصوص دالة على تأبيد دوامهم وانقطاع دوامهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duration formula is figurative hyperbole, using the expression Arabs conventionally used for perpetuity.
rows.anchor: بل التعبير عن التأبيد والمبالغة بما كانت العرب يعبرون به عنه على سبيل التمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even literal linkage would not entail that ending the heavens ends punishment or that punishment’s duration entails everlasting heavens; implication cannot outweigh explicit wording.
rows.anchor: ولو كان للارتباط لم يلزم أيضا من زوال السموات والأرض زوال عذابهم ولا من دوامه دوامهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative means the heavens and earth of the afterlife, supported by the earth’s transformation and the need for shade and shelter there.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد سموات الآخرة وأرضها ويدل عليه قوله تعالى: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī objects that most people do not know the afterlife heavens’ existence and permanence; those who know already know reward and punishment endure, so the analogy adds nothing.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر لأنه تشبيه بما لا يعرف أكثر الخلق وجوده ودوامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception from remaining in Hell covers sinful monotheists who are eventually brought out; cessation for some suffices for an exception.
rows.anchor: استثناء من الخلود في النار لأن بعضهم وهم فساق الموحدين يخرجون منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second exception refers to those same believers, separated from Paradise during punishment; a fixed starting point also qualifies perpetuity.
rows.anchor: وهم المراد بالاستثناء الثاني فإنهم مفارقون عن الجنة أيام عذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division into wretched and blessed remains sound: it covers all at the gathering, while both states may coexist in one person in different respects.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك الشرط حيث التقسيم لانفصال حقيقي أو مانع من الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Hell’s people sometimes move to the bitter cold or other torments, while Paradise’s people receive higher bliss such as divine pleasure, vision, and nearness to the Holy Presence.
rows.anchor: أو لأن أهل النار ينقلون منها إلى الزمهرير وغيره من العذاب أحيانا، وكذلك أهل الجنة ينعمون بما هو أعلى من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may cover waiting for judgment, since the wording places them in Hell when the Day comes; if duration is unrestricted to that Day, it may cover worldly life and the barzakh.
rows.anchor: أو من أصل الحكم والمستثنى زمان توقفهم في الموقف للحساب لأن ظاهره يقتضي أن يكونوا في النار حين يأتي اليوم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported analysis makes the exception apply to their groaning and gasping.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من قوله: { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported reading gives illā the sense of siwā, an endless addition beyond the heavens’ and earth’s duration.
rows.anchor: وقيل إلا ها هنا بمعنى سوى كقولك على ألف إلا الألفان القديمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God carries out whatever He wills without opposition.
rows.anchor: { إن ربك فعال لما يريد } من غير اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unsevered gift explicitly says reward does not end and shows the exception does not mean its cessation; reward and punishment are phrased differently to mark permanence.
rows.anchor: غير مقطوع، وهو تصريح بأن الثواب لا ينقطع وتنبيه على أن المراد من الاستثناء في الثواب ليس الانقطاع

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: They read سعدوا as passive, from سعده الله, meaning God made them happy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص { سعدوا } على البناء للمفعول من سعده الله بمعنى أسعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ is accusative either as an emphatic verbal noun, or as a circumstantial accusative from Paradise.
rows.anchor: و { عطاء } نصب على المصدر المؤكد أي أعطوا عطاء أو الحال من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not doubt that polytheist worship is misguidance leading to the fate of earlier idolaters, or that their objects of worship can harm but not benefit.
rows.anchor: { فلا تك فى مرية } شك بعد ما أنزل عليك من مآل أمر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubt concerns either the misguidance of their worship or the state of what they worship, which harms but does not benefit.
rows.anchor: من عبادة هؤلاء المشركين في أنها ضلال مؤد إلى مثل ما حل بمن قبلهم

words: مَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُهُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains the warning: they and their fathers share shirk; it can mean their worship matches their fathers’ or that they worship the same idols.
rows.anchor: { ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد ءاباؤهم من قبل } استئناف معناه تعليل النهي عن المرية أي هم وآباؤهم سواء في الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense sense, as their fathers used to worship, is elided but indicated by min qabl.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { كما يعبد } كما كان يعبد فحذف للدلالة من قبل عليه

words: مَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُهُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the causes of their and their fathers’ idolatry match, the same consequences and fate will follow.
rows.anchor: وقد بلغك ما لحق آباءهم من ذلك فسيلحقهم مثله، لأن التماثل في الأسباب يقتضي التماثل في المسببات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their share may mean punishment like their fathers’ or provision; the latter explains delayed punishment despite its cause.
rows.anchor: حظهم من العذاب كآبائهم، أو من الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial qualifier of their share, limiting full delivery; Arabic may figuratively say someone received his due even when only part was delivered.
rows.anchor: حال من النصيب لتقييد التوفية فإنك تقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen is what the senses cannot perceive.
rows.anchor: { علم الغيب } الغائب عن الحس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest is what is present to the senses.
rows.anchor: { والشهدة } الحاضر له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Great is so majestic that nothing falls outside His knowledge.
rows.anchor: { الكبير } العظيم الشأن الذي لا يخرج عن علمه شيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Exalted is supreme over all by power, or too exalted to bear created attributes.
rows.anchor: { المتعال } المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته، أو الذي كبر عن نعت المخلوقين وتعالى عنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who conceals speech keeps it within himself; one who makes it public speaks to another.
rows.anchor: { سواء منكم من أسر القول } في نفسه. { ومن جهر به } لغيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one hidden at night seeks concealment in a nighttime hiding place.
rows.anchor: { ومن هو مستخف بالليل } طالب للخفاء في مختبأ بالليل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib means appearing openly by day, from saraba, to emerge.
rows.anchor: { وسارب } بارز. { بالنهار } يراه كل أحد من سرب سروبا إذا برز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib may coordinate with man or mustakhfin, treating man as dual, as in the cited line where two companions are meant.
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على من أو مستخف على أن من في معنى الإثنين كقوله:

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line uses man to mean two people, supporting the dual construction.
rows.anchor: نكن مثل من يا ذئب يصطحبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects to the preceding description and confirms God’s complete and comprehensive knowledge.
rows.anchor: والآية متصلة بما قبلها مقررة لكمال علمه وشموله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra has fifty-two verses.
rows.anchor: وهي آياتها اثنتان وخمسون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means: this is a book.
rows.anchor: { الر كتاب } أي هو كتاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through calling people to what the book contains, the Prophet brings them out of darkness into light.
rows.anchor: { أنزلنه إليك لتخرج الناس } بدعائك إياهم إلى ما تضمنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darknesses are the various kinds of misguidance.
rows.anchor: { من الظلمت } من أنواع الضلال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is guidance.
rows.anchor: { إلى النور } إلى الهدى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission means God’s enabling and facilitation, metaphorically borrowed from permission as the easing of a barrier.
rows.anchor: { بإذن ربهم } بتوفيقه وتسهيله مستعار من الاذن الذي هو تسهيل الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may attach to li-tukhrij or function circumstantially with its subject or object.
rows.anchor: وهو صلة { لتخرج } أو حال من فاعله أو مفعوله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path phrase may be an appositive to the light with the preposition repeated, or a fresh answer to an implied question.
rows.anchor: { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد } بدل من قوله: { إلى النور } بتكرير العامل أو استئناف على أنه جواب لمن يسأل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is attributed to God because He is its destination or makes it manifest.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الصراط إلى الله تعالى إما لأنه مقصده أو المظهر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These attributes signal that the path’s traveler will not be humiliated or disappointed.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الوصفين للتنبيه على أنه لا يذل سالكه ولا يخيب سابله

words: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks protection from the idols’ misguidance, attributing it to them causally as worldly life is said to have deluded people.
rows.anchor: فلذلك سألت منك العصمة واستعذت بك من إضلالهن

words: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal attribution echoes the statement that worldly life deluded them.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى: وغرتهم الحيوة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever follows Abraham’s religion is of him, a part of him inseparable in religious matters.
rows.anchor: { فمن تبعنى } على ديني. { فإنه منى } أي بعضي لا ينفك في أمر الدين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can forgive the disobedient from the outset or after enabling repentance; this supports that any sin, even shirk, may be forgiven, though the threat distinguishes it from other sins.
rows.anchor: تقدر أن تغفر له وترحمه ابتداء، أو بعد التوفيق للتوبة. وفيه دليل على أن كل ذنب فلله أن يغفره حتى الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min means some descendants or descendants of descendants; the object is omitted and means Ishmael and his line, whose settlement is implied by settling him.
rows.anchor: { ربنا إنى أسكنت من ذريتى } أي بعض ذريتي أو ذرية من ذريتي فحذف المفعول وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barren valley is rocky Mecca, which does not grow crops.
rows.anchor: { بواد غير ذى زرع } يعني وادي مكة فإنها حجرية لا تنبت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The House is forbidden to violate or neglect, or has always been revered and feared by tyrants.
rows.anchor: { عند بيتك المحرم } الذي حرمت التعرض له والتهاون به، أو لم يزل معظما ممنعا يهابه الجبابرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Flood was kept from overtaking the House, hence its name ʿatīq, freed from it.
rows.anchor: أو منع منه الطوفان فلم يستول عليه ولذلك سمي عتيقا أي أعتق منه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abraham prayed before arriving, the wording may refer to what had been or to what would later come to be.
rows.anchor: ولو دعا بهذا الدعاء أول ما قدم فلعله قال ذلك باعتبار ما كان أو ما سيؤول إليه.

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: A report says Sarah gave Hajar to Abraham; after Hajar bore Ishmael and Sarah became jealous, Abraham settled them at Mecca, Zamzam appeared, Jurhum found them by following birds, exchanged milk for water, and Hajar agreed.
rows.anchor: روي أن هاجر كانت لسارة رضي الله عنها فوهبتها لإبراهيم عليه السلام فولدت منه إسماعيل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is purposive and attaches to settled: Abraham settled them in the barren valley solely so they could establish prayer at the House.
rows.anchor: اللام لام كي وهي متعلقة ب { أسكنت } أي ما أسكنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the address shows prayer is the primary purpose of settling them; the prayer asks God to grant them success in it.
rows.anchor: وتكرير النداء وتوسيطه للاشعار بأنها المقصودة بالذات من إسكانهم ثمة، والمقصود من الدعاء توفيقهم لها.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām is imperative: Abraham asks God to enable them to pray.
rows.anchor: وقيل لام الأمر والمراد هو الدعاء لهم بإقامة الصلاة كأنه طلب منهم الإقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive: some human hearts; it is said asking for all hearts would have brought crowds of Persians and Romans and pilgrims among Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: و { من } للتبعيض ولذلك قيل لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليهم فارس والروم ولحجت اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, min marks origin, as in saying the heart is from me: hearts belonging to people.
rows.anchor: أو للابتداء كقولك: القلب مني سقيم أي أفئدة ناس.

rows.speaker: هشام
rows.claim: Hisham, with a reported qualification, reads afʾīdah with an added yāʾ after the hamza.
rows.anchor: بخلف عنه بياء بعد الهمزة

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A variant āfidah may be metathesized from afʾidah or mean groups that hasten toward the family.
rows.anchor: اسم فاعل من أفدت الرحلة إذا عجلت أي جماعة يعجلون نحوهم

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: Another variant drops the hamza for ease and may derive from afada.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الوجه فيه إخراجهما بين ويجوز أن يكون من أفد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts hasten toward them with longing and affection.
rows.anchor: { تهوى إليهم } تسرع إليهم شوقا وودادا.

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A passive reading means someone else inclines hearts toward them; another derives from hawiya, to love, made transitive by yearning.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تهوى } على البناء للمفعول من أهوى إليه غيره و { تهوى } من هوى يهوي إذا أحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the barren valley, God answered by making it a secure sanctuary supplied with fruits of every kind, even fruits of every season on one day.
rows.anchor: فأجاب الله عز وجل دعوته فجعله حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء حتى توجد فيه الفواكه الربيعية والصيفية والخريفية في يوم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their hidden and open states, interests, and needs, and is more merciful than they are to themselves; prayer expresses servitude, dependence on mercy, and eagerness for what He has.
rows.anchor: تعلم سرنا كما تعلم علننا، والمعنى إنك أعلم بأحوالنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they hide grief at separation and openly show supplication and reliance on God.
rows.anchor: ما نخفي من وجد الفرقة وما نعلن من التضرع إليك والتوكل عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the invocation intensifies pleading and turning to God.
rows.anchor: وتكرير النداء للمبالغة في التضرع واللجأ إلى الله تعالى.

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing is hidden from God because His essential knowledge relates equally to every object of knowledge; min denotes totality.
rows.anchor: لأنه العالم بعلم ذاتي يستوي نسبته إلى كل معلوم، ومن للاستغراق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks to perform prayer properly and regularly.
rows.anchor: { رب اجعلنى مقيم الصلوة } معدلا لها مواظبا عليها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase coordinates with the object of make me and is partitive, because revelation or past peoples show that some descendants will be unbelievers.
rows.anchor: عطف على المنصوب في { اجعلنى } ، والتبعيض لعلمه بإعلام الله أو استقراء عادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accept my supplication means either answer my prayer or accept my worship.
rows.anchor: { ربنا وتقبل دعاء } واستجب دعائي أو وتقبل عبادتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is steadied in knowing God sees their states and deeds and will punish them; alternatively the warning addresses anyone who imagines God neglects them through ignorance or delusion at respite.
rows.anchor: { ولا تحسبن الله غفلا عما يعمل الظلمون } خطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمراد به تثبيته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the verse as comfort for the oppressed and a threat to the oppressor.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه تسلية للمظلوم وتهديد للظالم.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb with nūn: We delay them.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو بالنون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes stare without settling in their sockets, overwhelmed by what they see.
rows.anchor: أي تشخص فيه أبصارهم فلا تقر في أماكنها من هول ما ترى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhtiʿīn means either hastening toward the caller or facing him with unblinking eyes in awe; the root conveys turning toward something.
rows.anchor: { مهطعين } أي مسرعين إلى الداعي، أو مقبلين بأبصارهم لا يطرفون هيبة وخوفا، وأصل الكلمة هو الإقبال على الشيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have their heads raised.
rows.anchor: { مقنعي رؤوسهم } رافعيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes remain fixed without blinking, or their gaze does not return so they can look at themselves.
rows.anchor: { لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم } بل تثبت عيونهم شاخصة لا تطرف، أو لا يرجع إليهم نظرهم فينظروا إلى أنفسهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts are empty of understanding from bewilderment; Arab usage calls a fool or coward empty-hearted, without judgment or strength.
rows.anchor: خلاء أي خالية عن الفهم لفرط الحيرة والدهشة

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line about a hyena’s chest being hollow attests the sense of empty or hollow.
rows.anchor: قال زهير: من الظلمان جؤجؤه هواء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says their hearts are empty of good and hollow of truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل خالية عن الخير خاوية عن الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to warn is addressed to Muhammad; the day is either Resurrection or death, the first day of their punishment.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة، أو يوم الموت فإنه أول أيام عذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is the second object of warn.
rows.anchor: وهو مفعول ثان ل { أنذر }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who did wrong are the polytheists and deniers.
rows.anchor: { فيقول الذين ظلموا } بالشرك والتكذيب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for punishment to be delayed, for return to worldly life until a near term, or for their lives to be extended briefly so they can believe and answer the call.
rows.anchor: أخر العذاب عنا أو ردنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا إلى حد من الزمان قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise is a response to the command, as in the parallel construction in 63:10.
rows.anchor: { نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل } جواب للأمر ونظيره لولا أخرتنى إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصلحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are understood as reported speech, and mā lakum is the oath’s response; direct address matches its grammatical form rather than indirect quotation.
rows.anchor: { أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال } على إرادة القول و { ما لكم } جواب القسم جاء بلفظ الخطاب على المطابقة دون الحكاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had sworn they would remain in this world, never removed by death, perhaps from arrogance or delusion as suggested by sturdy buildings and distant hopes.
rows.anchor: أقسمتم أنكم باقون في الدنيا لا تزالون بالموت،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they swore they would not move to another abode after death, remaining in the same state through a further stage.
rows.anchor: وقيل أقسموا أنهم لا ينتقلون إلى دار أخرى وأنهم إذا ماتوا لا يزالون على تلك الحالة إلى حالة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No community can anticipate its appointed term or be delayed beyond it.
rows.anchor: { ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is masculine because ummah is treated according to its meaning, the people.
rows.anchor: وتذكير ضمير { أمة } فيه للحمل على المعنى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They address the Prophet with this title mockingly, then call him insane for claiming God sent down the Reminder, the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: نادوا به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على التهكم، ألا ترى إلى ما نادوه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their charge means that claiming God sent down the Qur’an is the speech of a madman.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إنك لتقول قول المجانين حين تدعي أن الله تعالى نزل عليك الذكر، أي القرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt echoes Pharaoh’s accusation that the messenger sent to him was mad.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك قول فرعون: إن رسولكم الذى أرسل إليكم لمجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawmā combines law with mā, bringing together an unreal condition and an exhortation.
rows.anchor: ركب { لو } مع { ما } كما ركبت مع لا لمعنيين امتناع الشيء لوجود غيره والتحضيض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand angels either to confirm and support the Prophet or to bring punishment for their denial, as with earlier nations.
rows.anchor: ليصدقوك ويعضدوك على الدعوة كقوله تعالى: لولا أنزل إليه ملك فيكون معه نذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand is conditional on the Prophet’s truthfulness claim.
rows.anchor: { إن كنت من الصدقين } في دعواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading makes angels an accusative object with God implied as subject; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read with nūn, while Abū Bakr reads passive with angels nominative.
rows.anchor: بالياء ونصب { الملئكة } على أن الضمير لله تعالى

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A further reading, تنزل, means they descend successively.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تنزل } بمعنى تتنزل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend only as wisdom determines; visible appearance would confuse people, and hastening punishment would destroy those destined for faith, including in their descendants.
rows.anchor: { إلا بالحق } إلا تنزيلا ملتبسا بالحق أي بالوجه الذي قدره واقتضته حكمته، ولا حكمة في أن تأتيكم بصور تشاهدونها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, truth here means revelation or punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحق الوحي أو العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhan answers them, with an understood condition: if angels descended, they would not be granted respite.
rows.anchor: { إذا } جواب لهم وجزاء لشرط مقدر أي ولو نزلنا الملائكة ما كانوا منظرين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic declaration rebuts their denial and mockery, affirming that God sent down the Reminder.
rows.anchor: رد لإنكارهم واستهزائهم ولذلك أكده من وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protects the Qur’an from alteration, additions, and omissions by making its inimitable wording distinguishable from human speech to Arabic speakers.
rows.anchor: أي من التحريف والزيادة والنقص بأن جعلناه معجزا مباينا لكلام البشر، بحيث لا يخفى تغيير نظمه على أهل اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse guarantees that the Qur’an will remain free of error over time.
rows.anchor: أو نفي تطرق الخلل إليه في الدوام بضمان الحفظ له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative takes the pronoun to refer to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير في { له } للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the angels He will create a human from ringing clay formed from altered mud.
rows.anchor: عدلت خلقته وهيأته لنفخ الروح فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To shape Adam is to proportion his form and prepare it for the spirit.
rows.anchor: { فإذا سويته } عدلت خلقته وهيأته لنفخ الروح فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit first attaches to subtle vapor from the heart, receives life, and travels through the arteries and body; its relation to the body is called blowing because air passes into another body’s cavity.
rows.anchor: وأصل النفخ إجراء الريح في تجويف جسم آخر، ولما كان الروح يتعلق أولا بالبخار اللطيف المنبعث من القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit’s attribution to God follows the explanation given in al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الروح إلى نفسه لما مر في «النساء».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-qaʿū means fall down before him; it is the imperative of waqaʿa.
rows.anchor: فاسقطوا له. { سجدين } أمر من وقع يقع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question denies equivalence after proofs of God’s power, wisdom, and exclusive creation; one unable to create cannot share His divinity.
rows.anchor: إنكار بعد إقامة الدلائل المتكاثرة على كمال قدرته وتناهي حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected comparison would ask whether the non-creator equals the Creator; reversing it highlights that idolatry makes God seem like powerless created beings.
rows.anchor: وكان حق الكلام أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق، لكنه عكس تنبيها على أنهم بالإشراك بالله سبحانه وتعالى جعلوه من جنس المخلوقات العجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do not create include every being worshipped besides God, rational beings or idols; they are treated as rational because called gods, or for stylistic matching and emphasis.
rows.anchor: والمراد بمن لا يخلق كل ما عبد من دون الله سبحانه وتعالى مغلبا فيه أولو العلم منهم أو الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should recognize the error because it is so evident that slight recollection and attention suffice.
rows.anchor: فإنه لجلائه كالحاصل للعقل الذي يحضر عنده بأدنى تذكر والتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are the deities people worship.
rows.anchor: { والذين يدعون من دون الله } أي والآلهة الذين تعبدونهم من دونه.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وحفص
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads yadʿūn with yāʾ; Ḥafṣ reads all three occurrences in this passage with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر «يدعون» بالياء. وقرأ حفص ثلاثتها بالياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because these deities create nothing, they cannot share God’s divinity; as contingent beings they depend on creation, whereas a deity must exist necessarily.
rows.anchor: لما نفى المشاركة بين من يخلق ومن لا يخلق بين أنهم لا يخلقون شيئا لينتج أنهم لا يشاركونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people possess is the transient goods of this world, and it runs out.
rows.anchor: { ما عندكم } من أعراض الدنيا. { ينفد } ينقضي ويفنى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is with God is the inexhaustible store of His mercy; this explains the prior judgment and proves Paradise’s bliss endures.
rows.anchor: { وما عند الله } من خزائن رحمته. { باق } لا ينفد، وهو تعليل للحكم السابق ودليل على أن نعيم أهل الجنة باق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient endure deprivation and unbelievers’ harm, or the burdens of religious duties.
rows.anchor: على الفاقة وأذى الكفار، أو على مشاق التكاليف.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read the verb with nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم بالنون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recompense is for the best of their deeds, such as obligations and recommended acts, or is better than their deeds.
rows.anchor: بما يرجح فعله من أعمالهم كالواجبات والمندوبات، أو بجزاء أحسن من أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Depending on how Ṭā Hā is parsed, the clause can be its predicate, an oath’s answer, its vocative answer, or a resumption; Qur’an may resume Ṭā Hā as antecedent.
rows.anchor: خبر { طه } إن جعلته مبتدأ على أنه مؤول بالسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not send the Qur’an to make the Prophet suffer through excessive grief at Quraysh’s disbelief, since his duty is only to convey.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتتعب بفرط تأسفك على كفر قريش إذ ما عليك إلا أن تبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse does not burden him with excessive spiritual discipline, long night vigils, and standing for worship.
rows.anchor: أو بكثرة الرياضة وكثرة التهجد والقيام على ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaqāʾ commonly means toil, as in the proverb about a horse trainer and a chief being most burdened; the wording implies the Qur’an was sent to make him blessed.
rows.anchor: والشقاء شائع بمعنى التعب ومنه أشقى من رائض المهر، وسيد القوم أشقاهم. ولعله عدل إليه للإشعار بأنه أنزل عليه ليسعد.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the verse rebuts unbelievers who saw his worship and claimed he suffered by leaving their religion and receiving the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقيل رد وتكذيب للكفرة، فإنهم لما رأوا كثرة عبادته قالوا إنك لتشقى بترك ديننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means rather a reminder, as a disconnected exception; it cannot be an appositive to li-tashqā because the categories differ, nor a second direct purpose of one verb.
rows.anchor: { إلا تذكرة } لكن تذكيرا، وانتصابها على الاستثناء المنقطع، ولا يجوز أن يكون بدلا من محل { لتشقى } لاختلاف الجنسين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a verbal noun used circumstantially, or a purpose attached to Qur’an through an understood adjective.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو مصدر في موقع الحال من الكاف أو القرآن، أو مفعول له على أن { لتشقى } متعلق بمحذوف هو صفة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single verb cannot directly take two purpose clauses.
rows.anchor: فإن الفعل الواحد لا يتعدى إلى علتين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder benefits a tender-hearted person affected by warning, or one God knows will fear when warned.
rows.anchor: { لمن يخشى } لمن في قلبه خشية ورقة تتأثر بالإنذار، أو لمن علم الله منه أنه يخشى بالتخويف منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if one raises one’s voice in remembrance or invocation, God knows the secret and what is more hidden, the self’s inward thought; He does not need loud speech.
rows.anchor: أي وإن تجهر بذكر الله ودعائه فاعلم أنه غني عن جهرك فإنه سبحانه يعلم السر وأخفى منه، وهو ضمير النفس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public remembrance shapes it in the self, prevents distraction, and humbles the worshipper; it is not to inform God.
rows.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على أن شرع الذكر والدعاء والجهر فيما ليس لإعلام الله بل لتصوير النفس بالذكر ورسوخه فيها ومنعها عن الاشتغال بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from God’s complete attributes to affirm that He alone possesses their implications.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه لما ظهر بذلك أنه المستجمع لصفات الألوهية بين أنه المتفرد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question awakens Moses’ attention to the wonders God will show through the staff.
rows.anchor: { وما تلك } استفهام يتضمن استيقاظا لما يريه فيها من العجائب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-yamīnika may be circumstantial to the demonstrative’s meaning or attached to tilka.
rows.anchor: { بيمينك } حال من معنى الإشارة، وقيل صلة { تلك }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating Moses’ name increases familiarity and draws attention.
rows.anchor: { يا موسى } تكرير لزيادة الاستئناس والتنبيه.

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: Aṣī is a dialectal reading of the Hudhayl tribe.
rows.anchor: على لغة هذيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses leans on the staff when tired or when standing at the head of the flock.
rows.anchor: { أتوكؤا عليها } أعتمد عليها إذا أعييت أو وقفت على رأس القطيع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He shakes leaves from branches over his sheep; the reading is related to brittle bread breaking apart.
rows.anchor: { وأهش بها على غنمى } وأخبط الورق بها على رؤوس غنمي، وقرىء { أهش } وكلاهما من هش الخبز يهش إذا انكسر لهشاشته

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A reading with sīn derives from driving sheep and means directing them with the staff.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالسين من الهس وهو زجر الغنم أي أنحى عليها زاجرا لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other uses include carrying tools, hanging a garment for shade, extending a short rope, and fighting predators threatening the sheep.
rows.anchor: إذا سار ألقاها على عاتقه فعلق بها أدواته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses understood the question as inviting the staff’s identity and ordinary uses, so he stated its nature and benefits before its transformation.
rows.anchor: وكأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم فهم أن المقصود من السؤال أن يذكر حقيقتها وما يرى من منافعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its later feats, including light, a bucket, lengthening, defense, water, leaves, and fruit, are signs created by God, not inherent properties.
rows.anchor: على أن ذلك آيات باهرة ومعجزات قاهرة أحدثها الله فيها لأجله وليست من خواصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses saw the staff as a fast-moving snake swallowing stones and trees, became afraid, and fled, so God told him to take it without fear.
rows.anchor: فإنه لما رآها حية تسرع وتبتلع الحجر والشجر خاف وهرب منها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means its former form and state.
rows.anchor: هيئتها وحالتها المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative may follow an elided preposition, or the causative may derive from ʿāda, to return.
rows.anchor: وانتصابها على نزع الخافض أو على أن أعاد منقول من عاده بمعنى عاد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is adverbial: God will return it to its former way.
rows.anchor: أو على الظرف أي سنعيدها في طريقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse estimates a verb: the staff will move as before and remain useful as before.
rows.anchor: أو على تقدير فعلها أي سنعيد العصا بعد ذهابها تسير سيرتها الأولى فتنتفع بها ما كنت تنتفع قبل.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says Moses’ heart calmed, and he put his hand into the snake’s mouth and grasped its jaws.
rows.anchor: قيل لما قال له ربه ذلك اطمأنت نفسه حتى أدخل يده في فمها وأخذ بلحييها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the great mission, Moses asks for a heart able to bear its burdens, hardship, and revelation, and for God to ease it by creating means and removing obstacles.
rows.anchor: لما أمره الله بخطب عظيم وأمر جسيم سأله أن يشرح صدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial li leaves what should be expanded or eased implicit, then naming the breast and matter makes the request emphatic.
rows.anchor: وفائدة لي إبهام المشروح والميسر أولا، ثم رفعه بذكر الصدر والأمر تأكيدا ومبالغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Effective conveyance is best done by an eloquent speaker; Moses asks to remove a speech impediment.
rows.anchor: فإنما يحسن التبليغ من البليغ وكان في لسانه رتة من جمرة أدخلها فاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says infant Moses pulled Pharaoh’s beard; Asiya argued he could not distinguish coal from ruby, and he put a coal in his mouth, causing the speech impediment.
rows.anchor: إنه صبي لا يفرق بين الجمر والياقوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī suggests the whitening of Moses’ hand may have been connected with this incident.
rows.anchor: ولعل تبييض يده كان لذلك.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says fire burned Moses’ hand, Pharaoh’s treatment failed, and Moses later pointed to the God who healed it.
rows.anchor: وقيل احترقت يده فاجتهد فرعون في علاجها فلم تبرأ، ثم لما دعاه قال إلى أي رب تدعوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreters disagree whether the impediment disappeared fully: some cite God granting Moses his request; others cite his later claim to be less eloquent and the taunt that he barely speaks.
rows.anchor: واختلف في زوال العقدة بكمالها فمن قال به تمسك بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī reconciles the evidence: Moses asked only to remove the impediment to understanding, not every speech defect; the indefinite knot marks the limited request.
rows.anchor: وأجاب عن الأول بأنه لم يسأل حل عقدة لسانه مطلقا بل عقدة تمنع الإفهام ولذلك نكرها وجعل يفقهوا جواب الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min lisānī may qualify uqdatun or attach to uḥlul.
rows.anchor: ومن لساني يحتمل أن يكون صفة عقدة وأن يكون صلة احلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs here are Moses’ miracles.
rows.anchor: { اذهب أنت وأخوك بئايتى } بمعجزاتي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means do not slacken or fall short.
rows.anchor: { ولا تنيا } ولا تفترا ولا تقصرا

rows.speaker: قُرئ
rows.claim: A reading uses kasra on the tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تنيا } بكسر التاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must remember God wherever they go and not forget Him.
rows.anchor: { فى ذكرى } لا تنسياني حيثما تقلبتما.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command means to proclaim God’s remembrance and call people to Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل في تبليغ ذكري والدعاء إلي.
